h1: Land Rover Repair vs Full Rebuild
lede: Understand the difference between a targeted engine repair and a comprehensive full rebuild - and decide which is right for your Land Rover.

blocks.html: In the workshop, an engine repair and a full rebuild are two fundamentally different approaches. A repair is targeted and localised - it fixes a specific issue with minimal disassembly. A full rebuild is a complete overhaul: the engine is stripped to its component parts, everything is inspected and machined where needed, and all wear items are replaced. The choice depends on the condition of your engine, its mileage, and how you use your vehicle.

items.q: When is a repair better than a full rebuild?
items.a: A repair is better when the problem is isolated - for example, a single leaking injector or a failed turbocharger - and the rest of the engine is in good condition. It's faster and cheaper, but it won't address underlying wear across the engine.

items.q: When does a full rebuild make more sense?
items.a: A full rebuild makes sense when the engine has multiple issues - timing chain wear, bearing wear, oil leaks - or when the engine has high mileage and the cost of individual repairs is approaching the cost of a rebuild. It restores the engine to like-new condition and typically comes with a 12-month warranty.

items.q: How much does a Land Rover engine repair cost?
items.a: Repairs start from around £1,900 for a 4-cylinder engine, depending on the scope. A full rebuild of a 6-cylinder diesel starts from £2,400. Every quote is fixed and transparent after inspection.

items.q: Do you offer a warranty on repairs and rebuilds?
items.a: Yes. All full rebuilds come with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Repairs are also warranted, but coverage depends on the specific work carried out.
